title: Applied anatomy: the thoracic inlet and diaphragm

related.why: Brachial plexus: the lower trunk a Pancoast tumour invades

brief.scenario: A 62-year-old man has a tumour at the apex of the right lung. He has pain in the right shoulder and inner arm, and wasting of the small muscles of the right hand. This is a verbal viva: the examiner will ask about the thoracic inlet, and will read out a description of the diaphragm viewed from below.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the thoracic inlet and diaphragm, including the written description the examiner reads out, and relate them to his presentation and to procedures in this region.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Ring of bone, what passes through it, what the tumour touches. Then three openings in the diaphragm.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Listing bones without the nerves that explain his symptoms.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The inlet is bounded by T1, the first ribs and the manubrium."

grid.label: Borders of the inlet
grid.pass: Body of T1 behind, first ribs and their cartilages at the sides, upper border of the manubrium in front.
grid.high: Adds the suprapleural membrane over the lung apex, which rises above the clavicle into the root of the neck.

grid.label: Contents
grid.fail: Names only the trachea and oesophagus.
grid.pass: Trachea, oesophagus, thoracic duct, lung apices, great arteries, brachiocephalic veins, vagus and phrenic nerves, sympathetic trunks.
grid.high: Scalene relations: subclavian vein in front of scalenus anterior; subclavian artery and plexus trunks behind; phrenic nerve on its front.

grid.label: Explains his presentation
grid.fail: Cannot explain the shoulder and hand symptoms.
grid.pass: Apical tumour invades the lower trunk (C8–T1): pain in shoulder and inner arm, wasting of the small hand muscles.
grid.high: Adds Horner's syndrome from the sympathetic chain; hoarseness on the right if the recurrent laryngeal nerve under the subclavian artery is involved.

grid.label: Structures at risk in procedures
grid.fail: Cannot name a structure at risk.
grid.pass: Pneumothorax during subclavian or jugular line insertion, because the apex rises into the neck; thoracic duct injury on the left causing a chyle leak.
grid.high: Adds phrenic nerve on scalenus anterior, and recurrent laryngeal nerves in the tracheo-oesophageal groove during thyroid or oesophageal surgery.

grid.label: Diaphragm openings
grid.fail: Cannot name the openings or their levels.
grid.pass: Caval (T8): IVC, right phrenic nerve. Oesophageal (T10): oesophagus, vagal trunks. Aortic (T12): aorta, thoracic duct, azygos vein.
grid.high: Aortic opening lies behind the median arcuate ligament, not through muscle; the caval opening widens on inspiration.

grid.label: Diaphragm in practice
grid.fail: Does not know the nerve supply of the diaphragm.
grid.pass: Motor supply from the phrenic nerve (C3–5): injury paralyses that hemidiaphragm; irritation refers pain to the shoulder tip.
grid.high: Congenital hernias: Bochdalek posterolateral, usually left; Morgagni anterior. Hiatus hernia: sliding or rolling.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What are the borders of the thoracic inlet?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What is at risk when you put in a subclavian line?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'm not sure; the artery, maybe.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Where does the oesophagus pass through the diaphragm?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What are the borders of the thoracic inlet?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The body of T1 behind, the first ribs and their cartilages at the sides, and the upper border of the manubrium in front.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The trachea, oesophagus and thoracic duct, the lung apices, the great arteries and the brachiocephalic veins, and the vagus and phrenic nerves and sympathetic trunks.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Why does he have these symptoms?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The tumour at the apex invades the lower trunk of the brachial plexus, C8 and T1. That gives shoulder and inner arm pain and wasting of the small muscles of the hand.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What is at risk in procedures here?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The lung apex rises into the neck, so a subclavian or jugular line can cause a pneumothorax. On the left, the thoracic duct can be injured and cause a chyle leak.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Name the openings in the diaphragm.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Caval at T8 with the IVC and right phrenic nerve. Oesophageal at T10 with the oesophagus and vagal trunks. Aortic at T12 with the aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The phrenic nerve, C3 to 5. Injury paralyses that half, and irritation refers pain to the shoulder tip.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The suprapleural membrane. The apex rises above the clavicle into the root of the neck.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How are the vessels arranged at the scalenes?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The subclavian vein lies in front of scalenus anterior. The subclavian artery and plexus trunks lie behind it. The phrenic nerve runs down its front.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What else might you find in him?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Horner's syndrome from the sympathetic chain. And because it's on the right, hoarseness if it reaches the recurrent laryngeal nerve where it hooks under the subclavian artery.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: In neck and thyroid surgery I'd also think of the phrenic nerve on scalenus anterior and the recurrent laryngeal nerves in the tracheo-oesophageal groove.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Does the aorta pass through the diaphragm muscle?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No, it passes behind the median arcuate ligament. The caval opening is in the central tendon and widens on inspiration.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Bochdalek is posterolateral and usually left-sided; Morgagni is anterior. Hiatus hernias are sliding or rolling.

failures.move: Not linking hand wasting to the lower trunk.
failures.consequence: Misses the anatomical basis of the presentation.

failures.move: Mixing up the levels of the openings.
failures.consequence: Undermines hiatus and aortic anatomy asked about next.

failures.move: Not knowing the lung apex rises into the neck.
failures.consequence: Misses why line insertion causes pneumothorax.

recovery.line: I 8 10 eggs at 12: IVC at T8, oesophagus at T10, aorta at T12.
Which structure at the inlet could produce that?

knowledge.fact: Inlet: T1 body, first ribs and cartilages, upper manubrium.
Openings: caval T8, oesophageal T10, aortic T12.
Apical tumour: lower trunk (C8–T1) pain and hand wasting; Horner's from the sympathetic chain.
Right recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under the right subclavian artery; left under the aortic arch.
Phrenic nerve C3–5 on scalenus anterior; diaphragm irritation refers pain to the shoulder tip.

recall.think: Which structure at the inlet explains each symptom?
recall.say: "The tumour is invading the lower trunk and the sympathetic chain."
recall.trap: Forgetting the lung apex sits above the clavicle.
recall.finish: Explain each symptom by the structure involved.

partner.opening: This is a verbal viva on the root of the neck and the diaphragm. What are the borders of the thoracic inlet?

reveals.finding: Read out: in a view of the diaphragm from below, there are three main openings. The most posterior lies in the midline, between the two crura, directly in front of the vertebral column. Ask: which opening is this, at what vertebral level, and what passes through it? Then name the other two openings.

push.question: What passes through the inlet?
push.expect: Trachea, oesophagus, thoracic duct, apices, great vessels, vagus and phrenic nerves, sympathetic trunks.

push.question: Why does he have hand wasting?
What is at risk in a subclavian line?
push.expect: Pleura and lung apex; on the left, the thoracic duct.

push.question: Name the openings in the diaphragm.
push.expect: T8 caval, T10 oesophageal, T12 aortic, with contents.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Right recurrent laryngeal nerve, which hooks under the right subclavian artery near the apex.

curveballs.prompt: After a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, a patient has right shoulder tip pain. Why?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Diaphragmatic irritation referred through the phrenic nerve (C3–5) to the shoulder.

curveballs.prompt: Milky fluid drains after a left neck dissection. What is it?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Chyle from a thoracic duct injury where it joins the left venous angle.
